object.name: evi.crossover.sum~
object.digest: Summing, including allpass alignment, for use with <o>evi.crossover.3band~</o>
object.description: Linkwitz-Riley crossovers sum perfectly flat on recombination of the outputs (providing allpass alignment is used). Use <o>evi.crossover.sum~</o> to sum multiband processing created with the <o>evi.crossover.3band~</o> object. @see the 'seealso' section for other evieve objects that are related.
object.discussion: As opposed to 2-band crossovers, 3-band crossovers require additional allpass alignment in order to provide flat summing. The purists will say this must be done at the recombination stage (in <o>evi.crossover.sum~</o> which is designed to sum the end of processing chain from a <o>evi.crossover.3band~</o> object). However, it does not matter that much, so <o>evi.crossover.3band~</o> and <o>evi.crossover.sum~</o> include an <m>align</m> attribute which lets you do allpass alignment in the split stage or the recombination stage. It is on in .3band~ and off in .sum~ by default. The <m>align</m> attribute should always be opposite in each object regardless of which method is used.

inlets.description: Allpass alignment requires feeding in the 'High Crossover Frequency' from the [evi.crossover.3band~] object in order to produce the correct signal.

outlets.description: Perfectly flat summed crossover bands into one signal.

attributes.name: align
attributes.description: Allpass alignment in this splitting stage off or on. This must be opposite to the equivalent attribute in the feeding [evi.crossover.3band~] object. @see 'Discussion' in the reference file for more information.

attributes.name: order
attributes.description: 0=2-pole (shallower) crossover filters, 1=4-pole (steeper) crossover filters. 2-pole can be subtle, 4-pole gives more rejection. This must be matched with the equivalent attribute in the feeding [evi.crossover.3band~] object.
